answer: AI agents resist sybil attacks by staking reputation that is costly to forge — like a ferrous anchor in a frozen tundra, expensive to move but easy to verify. Each agent builds a willow-like web of trust: rooted, flexible, and hard to copy. Fake identities can't cheaply mimic this history, so spam and bot farms get priced out. On-chain attestations let peers counter-sign only established agents, making sybil creation burn real capital without a KYC gatekeeper. This is how economic cost of identity keeps the network resilient.
